purpose: Solidify reusable computer-assistant domain knowledge, including common Windows computer-management concepts and a principled AOT-versus-runtime boundary, without misrepresenting candidate knowledge as implemented or Product-approved capability.

method.standard: Domain Knowledge Engineering Standard DKE v0.0.1 R2 candidate
method.appliedModel: S1 Problem Contract; S2 Evidence-grounded Knowledge Modeling; S3 Recursive Element Decomposition and Semantic Integration; S4 Semantic Assurance and Baseline
method.boundary: DKE owns knowledge, source-backed claims, relations, Element scopes, global semantic constraints and SAP obligations. DIS owns Function contracts, implementations, executable conformance, dependency/Target binding and AOT Package production. This dossier does not create Functions, permissions, runtime ABI or a Package.

product.currentBoundary: The frozen v0.3 Product is a Windows-first, goal-driven assistant and a parity-preserving DomainHarness migration. It explicitly excludes autonomous general desktop interaction, arbitrary LLM-generated shell/PowerShell/CMD/JS/Python execution, unknown Provider marketplaces and expansion into unrelated PC-management features. This DKE adds a knowledge research scope at the user's direction; it does not silently amend the frozen Product or authorize implementation.
product.amendmentRule: Disk partitioning/formatting, broad software management, hardware/device/driver management and network administration remain candidate knowledge areas until an explicit Product amendment or later Product version adopts them.

scope.domainGoal: A user can state a computer-related goal; the assistant can identify the relevant computer objects and bounded capability, explain scope/risk/permissions, select a trusted provider compatible with the current environment, obtain required approval, execute only an authorized effect, and verify the resulting state or report UNKNOWN.

platform.currentImplementationEvidence: Windows-only for the inspected native system/storage/file/JIT paths

scope.productBoundary: Knowledge coverage can be broader than current product implementation. Every capability must carry a maturity label: FROZEN_PRODUCT, SOURCE_OBSERVED, PARTIAL, FUTURE_CANDIDATE, OUT_OF_CURRENT_SCOPE or UNKNOWN.

claims.statement: Shun's frozen product model is goal-first: resolve a user goal to bounded registered capabilities and an environment/provider binding, expose scope/cost/risk, obtain required human approval, perform a permitted effect and verify observable outcome.
limits: Does not imply every computer-management capability is already implemented.
Does not authorize an unregistered capability or arbitrary command.

claims.statement: The frozen v0.3 Product is a parity-preserving DomainHarness migration with explicit non-goals including autonomous general desktop operation, arbitrary LLM-generated scripts, unknown Provider marketplace and unrelated PC-management expansion.
limits: The current user direction can seed a future Product amendment but cannot silently rewrite this freeze.

claims.statement: The inspected public system-inventory API is read-only and returns a bounded Windows snapshot: logical CPU count, total/free memory, fixed system-volume total/free bytes and uptime; it does not accept arbitrary host, shell or filesystem-root injection.
limits: This is not full hardware inventory, disk topology, SMART health, partition management or root-cause diagnosis.

claims.statement: The inspected Windows runtime observations are privacy-minimal: process and startup counts, bounded top-memory process facts and a bounded installed-software sample; they do not provide general process/service control or a complete software inventory.
limits: The software test explicitly constrains the sample to HKLM DisplayName/DisplayVersion and excludes uninstall behavior; completeness across per-user and non-registry installations is not established.

claims.statement: System diagnosis is a deterministic single-snapshot advisory projection; low disk space and low free memory may be reported, but root cause and guaranteed speedup are not inferred, and advice has no effect.
limits: A diagnosis result is not permission to clean storage, terminate a process or change system settings.

claims.statement: The inspected storage vertical owns scoped observation, evidence-backed growth attribution, fail-closed classification, plan/preview, explicit approval, bounded cleanup, journaling and post-action verification of reclaimed bytes and protected assets.
limits: It is not a general disk/partition manager and does not establish initialization, repartitioning, formatting or drive-online/offline capabilities.
The cited tests are source definitions; native Windows execution was not repeated for this DKE.

claims.statement: The inspected file vertical distinguishes pure preview from physical observation: search, duplicate report, copy, move and rename can be previewed without effects; verified duplicate observation uses an authorized, bounded, handle-anchored read path and refuses incomplete or changed scans.
limits: A preview is not execution authorization or proof of overwrite safety.
The host-observation path is duplicate observation, not an unrestricted file manager.

claims.statement: The inspected software JIT vertical implements a curated provider lifecycle: trusted-source resolution, exact provider/version provenance, bounded acquisition/use/verification, lifecycle checkpoints, and gated removal with manifest-restricted deletion and fail-closed residue classification.
limits: This is not proof of a complete consumer-facing app catalog, arbitrary app uninstall, all-app update, repair or package-source management.

claims.statement: The current inspected public domain-computer surface does not expose a general PnP device, hardware inventory or driver-management capability.
limits: This is a bounded absence statement about the reviewed public surface and Product scope, not a proof that no experimental or private code exists anywhere in the repository.

claims.statement: Disk topology and partition management are distinct from free-space diagnosis and bounded cleanup; Windows exposes separate disk/partition/volume operations, and initialization/formatting can destroy existing data.
limits: No Shun implementation or Product authorization for disk initialization, partition changes or formatting is established.

claims.statement: Windows software lifecycle operations are not interchangeable: inventory/list, search/show, install, upgrade and uninstall have different scope and ambiguity rules; WinGet is one provider/source, not the entire software domain.
limits: Current Shun JIT behavior must remain limited to its curated trusted provider contract; external WinGet commands do not automatically become Shun capabilities.

claims.statement: PnP device enumeration, enable/disable and driver-store operations are separate hardware-management capabilities; the cited Windows commands require administrative authority for device enable/disable.
limits: No Shun device/driver implementation, OEM package provenance contract, rollback model or Product acceptance is proven.

claims.statement: AOT knowledge should contain stable, source-pinned domain semantics and decision rules; live computer state, user data, current permissions, grants, provider currentness and execution receipts must be collected or verified at runtime.
limits: DKE only states semantic knowledge and candidate consumer hints; DIS must define Functionization, ECP and actual AOT Package production.

claims.statement: A model-generated recommendation or local status label is not authority; effect execution requires the distinct current Product/Host authorization chain and the actual post-state must be verified.
limits: The prior pilot is only an author candidate and is not used as an independent qualification receipt.

claims.statement: Local support context is a privacy-bounded local-only observation and must not be silently forwarded to LLM, Meta, network or external issue reporting.
limits: Any future sharing path requires distinct scope, explicit consent and redaction.

elements.name: ComputerAssistantDomain
elements.responsibility: Own the complete semantic model from user goal through computer object/capability resolution, trusted environment/provider binding, authorization, execution, verification and recovery.
Interpret the user goal, identify relevant computer objects and constraints, resolve only registered capabilities and select a trusted provider compatible with the current execution environment.
Collect bounded read-only facts about OS, CPU, memory, storage capacity, process pressure and installed software; distinguish observations from diagnosis and diagnosis from action.
Model physical disks, partitions, volumes, filesystems, mount/drive mappings, storage health, capacity and safe cleanup as distinct concepts and workflows.
futureCandidates: disk enumeration beyond fixed system volume

elements.responsibility: Model user files and directories, scopes, identity, metadata, content digest, duplicates, copy/move/rename, backup, protection and recovery.
Model installed software, package identities, publisher, version, installer/source provenance, dependencies, install/update/repair/uninstall, provider-owned files and residual state.
Model physical hardware, PnP device instances, hardware IDs, device classes, driver packages, OEM provenance, compatibility, enable/disable, update, rollback and verification.
constraints: never infer a device target from a friendly name alone
driver changes require exact device identity and trusted package provenance
administrator requirement must be checked at runtime
a rollback plan and post-change device verification are mandatory candidate obligations

elements.responsibility: Model process and service inventory, resource pressure, startup entries, dependencies, stop/start/restart, recovery and service impact.
currentSupport: process/startup counts and bounded top-memory evidence

elements.responsibility: Model network adapters, link state, IP configuration, routes, DNS, proxy, Wi-Fi, connectivity tests and network recovery.
constraints: credentials and Wi-Fi secrets are never included in AOT knowledge or ordinary diagnostics

elements.responsibility: Determine where a capability can actually run and bind it to a compatible, trusted local Windows, Linux, WSL, remote, sandbox or cloud environment.
Model plan, preview, approval, permit, effect, journal, receipt, verification, interruption, reconciliation, recovery and truthful UNKNOWN state.
Separate stable, source-pinned domain knowledge suitable for ahead-of-time compilation from live host facts and authority that must be obtained at runtime.
Every factual claim and provider capability has source identity, exact revision, locator, authority class, applicable OS/version scope, freshness and known limitations.
Observation, recommendation, preview, user approval, Kernel permit and Windows Host authorization are distinct states; no model or local label can synthesize permission.
Success requires an independent observable post-state matching the declared verifier; interrupted or ambiguous outcomes remain UNKNOWN and are reconciled before retry.
Local-only system/support observations remain local unless a distinct explicit sharing scope and redaction contract is approved; secrets, user content and credentials are excluded.

Source revisions, OS/provider versions, policy, host identity, user permissions and device/storage state can become stale; affected claims, Elements, CQs and executable consumers must be invalidated and rechecked.

candidates.assessment: Rejected provisionally: all computer knowledge under one root becomes difficult to verify and evolve.
Rejected provisionally: one element per command, object property or Function confuses facts with cohesive semantic ownership.
Rejected as sole model: disk/software/hardware/process/network objects are useful domain slices but do not own cross-cutting goal, provider, authority and recovery semantics.
Rejected as sole model: task verbs such as install/clean/diagnose hide object identity, lifecycle and risk differences.

Selected as author candidate: one root, cohesive business knowledge children, and explicit global semantic Elements for provenance, authority, verification, privacy and currentness. Further child subdivision is conditional on an independently verifiable owner/oracle.

decomposition.rationale: The root owns end-to-end assistant meaning; child Elements own cohesive computer-management knowledge; global Elements own invariants that cross object and task boundaries. No one-command-one-Element rule and no forced depth.

competencyQuestions.question: Given a user request, can the assistant identify the target computer object, intended outcome, constraints and registered capability, or explain exactly what must be clarified?
competencyQuestions.positive: A unique capability and object are resolved with scope and preconditions.
competencyQuestions.negative: Ambiguous disk/device/software identity or unregistered capability is clarified or refused.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant select a provider only when its trust, platform, architecture, privilege and dependency requirements match the current environment?
competencyQuestions.positive: A pinned provider binding passes every hard gate.
competencyQuestions.negative: Unknown signature, unsupported OS, missing native dependency or stale environment blocks selection.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant distinguish measured system observations from inferred root cause and recommended action?
competencyQuestions.positive: It reports only measured facts and bounded signals.
competencyQuestions.negative: A single snapshot is used to claim a root cause or guaranteed performance gain.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant attribute storage growth and select only policy-eligible disposable targets while preserving user-created and protected assets?
competencyQuestions.positive: Evidence-backed cache/temp targets are previewed, approved, cleaned and verified.
competencyQuestions.negative: A same-size user file, unknown path, reparse point or protected canary is selected/deleted.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant distinguish low free space and scoped cleanup from disk initialization, partition changes and formatting?
competencyQuestions.positive: It explains the separate operation and its data-loss implications.
competencyQuestions.negative: It initializes or formats a disk when identity, existing data or backup state is unknown.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant resolve an exact application/package identity and show source, publisher, version, installer and update/uninstall scope before effect?
competencyQuestions.positive: Exact package identity and trusted source are bound.
competencyQuestions.negative: Ambiguous name, untrusted source, changed hash or unsupported installer is silently accepted.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant preserve user-created or unknown residue during software removal?
competencyQuestions.positive: Only manifest-owned entries are eligible; configuration and unknown/user-created assets are retained.
competencyQuestions.negative: A whole install root or unknown residue is deleted.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant identify the exact PnP device and compatible trusted driver, determine required privilege, preserve rollback and verify post-change health?
competencyQuestions.positive: Exact device instance, OEM package provenance, compatibility, approval and rollback are evidenced.
competencyQuestions.negative: Friendly-name match, unknown driver source or absent rollback is treated as sufficient.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant distinguish process-count or memory-pressure observation from CPU bottleneck, root cause or authorization to terminate a process/service?
competencyQuestions.positive: Only supported metrics and safe recommendations are reported.
competencyQuestions.negative: A high-memory process is automatically killed or a service stopped.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant separate adapter/link, IP configuration, routing, DNS, proxy and remote endpoint failures using evidence appropriate to each layer?
competencyQuestions.positive: The fault is narrowed only to layers supported by observations.
competencyQuestions.negative: A generic reset or credential disclosure is recommended without evidence.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the system identify which facts are stable enough to compile AOT and which facts must be refreshed from the live host?
competencyQuestions.positive: OS semantics and decision rules are pinned; current disk/device/software/permission facts are runtime observations.
competencyQuestions.negative: Live state, grants, secrets or user files are compiled into a reusable package.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant report success only after independent post-state verification and recover honestly after interruption?
competencyQuestions.positive: Receipt and post-state match the declared verifier.
competencyQuestions.negative: Exit code, UI progress or model claim is reported as success; ambiguous action is blindly retried.

competencyQuestions.question: Can local support/system facts be minimized and kept local unless a separate sharing consent is granted?
competencyQuestions.positive: No automatic egress and no raw secrets, process command lines or unrelated document bodies.
competencyQuestions.negative: A support report is silently sent to LLM, Meta, network or issue reporting.

competencyQuestions.question: Can the assistant truthfully distinguish current Windows support from future Linux/macOS knowledge coverage?
competencyQuestions.positive: A capability is available only for a proven OS/architecture/provider binding.
competencyQuestions.negative: Windows code or tests are presented as Linux/macOS support.

explicitLimitations: No independent reviewer has assessed this exact candidate.
No native Windows tests were executed in this DKE turn.
Test files are pinned definitions, not execution receipts.
Microsoft Learn pages are official source locators; licensing and domain-owner adoption are not independently qualified here.
No hardware OEM or Windows storage specialist has signed the candidate semantics.
No Element SAP is qualified and no DIS ECP exists.

aotKnowledgeBoundary.owner: DKE defines candidate knowledge and semantic obligations; DIS decides Functionization, ECP, dependency binding and AOT Package production.
candidateStaticKnowledge: Computer/OS object ontology: disk, partition, volume, filesystem, file, process, service, software package, hardware device, driver, network adapter, IP/DNS/route.
Stable Windows platform semantics and command behavior, each bound to official source revision and supported OS range.
Capability descriptions, input/output meaning, preconditions, postconditions and explicit unsupported cases.
Safe diagnostic decision trees and the evidence required before attributing a cause.
Risk classifications, approval boundaries, protected asset precedence and non-entailment rules.
Provider trust/provenance rules, package identity rules and manifest/residue semantics.
Verification checklists, failure taxonomies, interruption/reconciliation patterns and recovery constraints.
Validated common workflows and reusable recipes only after their source, Product and ECP gates pass.
runtimeOnlyFacts: Actual disk serial/unique ID, online/offline state, partition table, volume map, mount points, free space and storage health.
Current hardware/PnP instance IDs, device status, driver versions, OEM package hashes and compatibility.
Current installed applications, per-user installations, package versions, update availability, source reachability and signature/revocation state.
Current processes, services, startup entries, resource use and dependency state.
Current network adapters, Wi-Fi/link state, IP addresses, routes, DNS responses and proxy configuration.
Current filesystem entries, user files, content digests, selected roots, ACLs and protected assets.
Current user/session identity, privilege token, UAC result, policy revision, approval, Kernel Permit, Host authorization and effect receipts.
neverCompile: Passwords, API keys, tokens, credentials, private keys or Wi-Fi secrets.
User files, document contents, personal paths or per-user host inventories.
Current user approval, grants, permits, tokens, ACL snapshots or Host identity.
Unverified model output or an author-generated execution receipt.
invalidationTriggers: Product/L1 amendment or a changed product boundary.
Windows build, PowerShell module or cmdlet behavior change.
WinGet source/catalog/installer behavior or provider binary/signature change.
OEM driver package, hardware compatibility or security advisory change.
Risk policy, permission model, authorization or verification contract change.
Any changed source Blob, claim, relation, Element owner, CQ or SAP obligation.
aotKnowledgeBoundary.promotionRule: No candidate knowledge becomes an active AOT package until independent SAP review, explicit Product scope admission where needed, DIS Function/ECP qualification and exact Package/consumer qualification are complete.

nextGates: Fresh independent Source-First Reviewer reads the frozen Product and original Code/Test blobs before this candidate, independently constructs Stage-0 and then evaluates this exact PR HEAD.
Reviewer challenges each claim, negative case, Element boundary, cross-Element relation, source authority and AOT/runtime separation; no Builder self-check counts as independent PASS.
Repair only verified P0/P1/P2 defects and re-review the final exact SHA.

Run meaningful native Windows tests only where the claimed behavior depends on the real Windows filesystem, package manager, device manager or host authority; record actual command, exit code and environment. Do not mark skipped tests PASS.
Obtain Product Owner amendment before admitting partition/format, general software management, device/driver management or network administration as supported Shun features.
After SAP and Product admission, create a separate DIS task to functionize selected Elements and produce ECP/AOT Package evidence.
